name: Dialog
intent: Focused modal task that interrupts the user with a backdrop and focus trap until it is completed or dismissed.
when: A task or confirmation must be finished before continuing
Content needs a backdrop and focus trap
Create/edit an entity without leaving the page (often hosting a Form)

chooseOver.because: Sheet is a side-anchored, often non-blocking panel for contextual work beside the page
Popover is lightweight, anchored to a trigger, and dismisses on outside click — not a blocking task
AlertDialog is the right modal for a destructive or irreversible confirmation

insteadUse.whenInstead: a transient success/error confirmation that needs no decision

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a plain Dialog for a destructive/irreversible confirmation
commonMistakes.symptom: No specialized affordance for dangerous actions

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a Dialog for small anchored content
commonMistakes.symptom: A heavy modal where a lightweight popover fits
commonMistakes.fix: Use a Popover for small anchored content
commonMistakes.avoidOverride: Use a Popover for small anchored content

commonMistakes.mistake: Overriding DialogHeader's shipped classes to get a lighter header
commonMistakes.symptom: Per-app drift: every consumer re-derives its own header and they stop matching

notes: Issue #248: the header went from stacked (0.2) to banded (0.13) with no opt-out, and a consumer's only route back was overriding shipped classes. The band stays the DEFAULT because it is a system decision rather than a dialog one — it is the same 40px bg-muted strip WidgetCardHeader and TableHeader draw, and reverting the dialog alone would leave it the only unbanded header in the library — but stacked is now a first-class variant, so the choice is per-dialog and documented instead of per-app and improvised. Flipping the default is one line in dialog.tsx if the design call goes the other way.

states.banded: The default. Header and footer are 40px bg-muted strips with a rule, deliberately identical to WidgetCardHeader (charts) and TableHeader (tables) so a modal reads as the same kind of object as every other panel; the close button centres in the header band and the footer steps its buttons down to h-7 to fit.
states.stacked: The pre-0.3 header: title over description, no band, no rule; the close button insets, the footer drops its strip and keeps full-size buttons, and the content is padded as one block. Right for a short dialog that is a sentence and two buttons rather than a panel.

usage: Use Dialog when you need to display content that temporarily overlays the main interface. This component is useful for focused interactions, confirmations, or supplementary information.
Dialog should be used sparingly as overlays interrupt the user's workflow. Reserve this component for important interactions that require user attention or action before continuing.

anatomy.description: Dialog is composed of the following parts:

parts.name: DialogTrigger
parts.description: Element that opens the dialog when activated.

parts.name: DialogContent
parts.description: Container for the dialog content and overlay.

parts.name: DialogHeader
parts.description: Header section containing title and description.

bestPractices.title: Focus management
bestPractices.description: Trap focus within the dialog and return focus when closed.

bestPractices.title: Don't nest dialogs
bestPractices.description: Avoid opening dialogs from within dialogs, use sequential flow instead.

bestPractices.title: Provide clear exit
bestPractices.description: Always include a visible close button and support Escape key.

bestPractices.title: Don't trap users
bestPractices.description: Never make dialogs impossible to close or require specific actions to dismiss.
bestPractices.example: // No close button or escape handling

bestPractices.title: Keep content focused
bestPractices.description: Limit dialog content to a single task or decision.

bestPractices.title: Don't overload dialogs
bestPractices.description: Avoid putting complex forms or multiple tasks in a single dialog.
